findings.failureScenario: Remote pools idle connections with no liveness check, while the server drops any connection idle past its 120 s read timeout (remote.rs:192). The engine keeps the loaded model, and so its Remote, for the next photo (denoise.rs `loaded`). If the user denoises a photo, waits more than 2 minutes, and starts another, every pooled connection is dead. Each try_run pops one, gets EOF ('the connection closed'), and counts a failure. With 4 slots, 3 failures reach MAX_FAILURES and the server is given up for the rest of the session: the remote GPU is never used again and the status shows 'given up', although the server is healthy.
findings.action: Treat an I/O failure on a pooled (reused) connection as a reconnect-and-retry on a fresh connection before counting a failure, or stamp pooled connections and drop them past an idle age below the server timeout. Consider resetting failures after a success.

findings.failureScenario: photo.duplicate stores the copy's hash as '<hash>:dup<id>' (convert.rs:343), and other code strips that suffix before comparing (missing.rs stored_hash, sync.rs base_hash). content_op compares the fresh probe hash against the stored, suffixed hash directly. So Reload from Disk on an unchanged duplicate always reports it as changed: it adds an undo step, drops its cached sources, and writes SetContent with the bare hash. That removes the ':dup' marker the duplicate relied on to avoid clashing with its original's content hash.
findings.action: Compare the base hash (strip the ':dupN' suffix, as missing.rs/sync.rs do) in content_op, and keep the suffix when the base hash is unchanged.

findings.failureScenario: The doc says is_unedited ignores only white balance 'as shot' values, but the code overwrites the whole wb (mode, temp, tint) with the defaults. Photo::is_edited is `*develop != defaults && !develop.is_unedited()`. So a photo whose only edit is a white-balance change (for example mode Custom at 3200 K) counts as unedited. It is missing from edited filters and smart rules, and lens_ops/import treat it as untouched.
findings.action: Ignore only the as-shot case: reset wb to default only when wb.mode == WbMode::AsShot (keeping mode/temp/tint comparisons otherwise).

findings.failureScenario: A render error is cached in `failed` under (slot, job key), and later requests with the same key are answered from the cache without rendering (render.rs:198). The only way to clear it for a live slot is Renderer::retry, and nothing in the repository calls it. A transient failure (a file briefly offline on an unmounted volume, or a memory-pressure decode error) therefore keeps replaying the same error for that photo and slot until the slot is evicted or the edit changes the key, even after the cause is gone.
findings.action: Wire retry into the host command surface (or clear failed entries on file/volume change and after a time-to-live), or cache only deterministic errors.

findings.failureScenario: estimate_cr3_framing fits the reference into the proxy's box with fit(), which keeps the reference's own aspect ratio, then returns None unless the size matches exactly. The comment on reference_at (398-402) records that this fit can round one pixel short (191x128 vs 192x128). When that happens, align_cr3_framing silently returns the unaligned sensor, so the CR3 framing correction is skipped for that file and the colour pairs are taken from misregistered pixels.
findings.action: Resize the reference to exactly (w, h) as reference_at does (`resize(reference, w, h, Filter::Box)`) instead of fit().

findings.failureScenario: MaxCLL is computed from the per-pixel max channel, but MaxFALL averages BT.2020 luminance. CTA-861.3 defines MaxFALL as the frame average of the per-pixel max(R,G,B); this is from the reviewer's recall and was not fetched. Saturated HDR content (a red highlight at 1000 nits has luminance of about 263) gets an understated MaxFALL in the PNG cLLI chunk and the AVIF content light level, which can make displays tone-map frames too brightly.
findings.action: Accumulate nits[0].max(nits[1]).max(nits[2]) into sum_nits (both the PNG and AVIF paths), matching the MaxCLL basis.
